steps: The new platform endpoint and existing event-audio starter options show exact ordinary GDScript source in Chinese, English and Japanese at 390px. Mode, path, focus, source and reachable Create/Cancel controls persist; cancelling writes nothing.
Create opens an ordinary unsaved TXT draft; Save adds exactly its source and registration while preserving all existing author files.

Manage existing behavior explicitly registers one script reference. The ordinary behavior editor adds one moving-platform binding and two event-name parameters, retains every consumer binding, and preserves focus/review in three languages. Cancel discards the first binding review. Apply changes only a draft; Save changes only the behavior JSON.
Reopening the saved behavior restores the same platform UUID, script identity and both literal event names. An unchanged review grants no Apply ticket and closing writes nothing.

The browser-authored ordinary publisher receives real endpoint notifications: destination then origin, with no startup origin event. Both carry the platform UUID and the new binding source. Destination triggers the existing animation and UUID-filtered audio consumer. Character carry still reverses and the independent character stays still; three-language event history remains readable at 390px.

Native support selects the exact moving-platform physics declaration. Event publisher, animation subscriber and audio subscriber independently open their frozen behavior binding sources with exact ranges when supplied. Navigation preserves the completed run and all author files after explicit Save.

events-ja.title: プロジェクトイベント履歴

limitations: Real HTTP editor and native Godot headless test; installed Tauri, Android and Bevy were not tested.

Runtime evidence covers native platform endpoint notifications published by an ordinary authored script, alongside executed animation and audio commands. Headless receipts do not prove audible output or audio hardware.

The browser creates one ordinary publisher TXT, registers one explicit reference and adds one platform binding with two event names. Media consumers are saved fixture scripts; no auto-binding or parameter discovery is claimed. This finite run uses the existing 128-publication project event budget.
